subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` be treated as a hard-enforced Telegram DM security boundary?
rationale: The schema and types already expose a security-sensitive DM policy surface, but current runtime enforcement does not read that direct config; enforcing or retiring it changes operator security expectations and config compatibility.

options.title: Enforce Direct DM Policy
options.body: Keep the existing config surface and implement direct-aware policy resolution with account, wildcard, thread, and sender-precedence regression coverage.

options.title: Retire The Accepted Surface
options.body: Reject or migrate the direct `tools` fields and document the supported alternative so operators do not rely on a silent no-op.

options.title: Defer To Broader Policy Design
options.body: Keep this issue open behind the broader route/session policy design, accepting that Telegram direct tool policy remains unreliable until that lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct DM Policy
recommendation.body: Keep the existing config surface and implement direct-aware policy resolution with account, wildcard, thread, and sender-precedence regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans config compatibility, Telegram direct behavior, and runtime tool-policy security, where current blame and recent history point most strongly to this owner.
